baseline:
B
A matrix is a way to encode a linear transformation. When a matrix is multiplied by a vector, it applies the transformation (such as a rotation, scaling, or shearing) to that vector, producing a new one.

C
A rotation matrix is a linear transformation that rotates a vector around the origin by a specific angle. This operation is an isometry, meaning it preserves the vector's length (magnitude).

C
Composition of transformations is the sequential application of one transformation followed by another on the result of the first.

C
The matrix product AB represents the composition of two linear transformations. Applying the resulting matrix AB to a vector x, written as (AB)x, is equivalent to A(Bx), which means applying the transformation for B first, then applying the transformation for A to the result.

C
The matrix product AB applied to a vector v, written as (AB)v, is equivalent to A(Bv). This means the transformation B is applied first, followed by transformation A.
